bull.b: The exclusive license creates potential recurring royalty income without requiring Loop to fund every facility directly. This could improve scalability and capital efficiency, although returns depend on ELITe building plants and generating sales.

Control over contracts, pricing and quantities gives Loop a direct role in commercializing recycled polymer products. Volume-linked marketing fees align Loop’s income with customer adoption and the long-term expansion of licensed production.

Technology that addresses difficult PET waste supports participation in the structural shift toward recycled materials and circular supply chains. Food-grade and high-purity outputs could broaden applications across packaging and textiles if commercial scale is achieved.

bear.b: Extremely negative margins and a very small, shrinking revenue base indicate that the current operating model is far from covering costs. Sustained losses limit internal funding capacity and make successful commercialization essential to future viability.

Ongoing operating and free-cash-flow losses require continued access to external funding or strategic capital. This can constrain investment in technology and facilities, while increasing dilution or financing risk before meaningful recurring revenue emerges.

The shift to negative equity shows that cumulative losses have materially eroded the capital base. Although total debt is modest, weak capitalization reduces financial flexibility and makes future funding, partnerships and facility development more difficult.
